name: Buda Castle
blurb: The royal palace atop Castle Hill, home to the National Gallery and the Budapest History Museum, with sweeping views over the Danube.

name: Fisherman's Bastion
blurb: Fairytale neo-Romanesque terraces and turrets with the best panorama of Parliament and the river.

name: Matthias Church
blurb: Gothic coronation church with a colourful Zsolnay-tiled roof, right beside the Fisherman's Bastion.

name: Citadella & Liberty Statue
blurb: Hilltop fortress crowned by the Liberty Statue, with a city view in every direction.

name: Gellért Baths
blurb: Art Nouveau thermal baths with mosaics, columns and a stunning indoor pool hall.

name: Rudas Baths
blurb: Ottoman-era bath from the 16th century with a rooftop pool overlooking the Danube.

name: Gellért Hill Cave Church
blurb: A chapel built into the cliff face of Gellért Hill, right by the river.

name: Széchenyi Chain Bridge
blurb: The first permanent bridge across the Danube, guarded by stone lions and lit beautifully at night.

name: Elizabeth Bridge
blurb: A sleek white suspension bridge named for Empress Sisi.

name: Liberty Bridge
blurb: Green iron bridge with turul birds on its pylons, a favourite for sunset views.

name: Margaret Bridge
blurb: Gateway to Margaret Island with a distinctive bend in the middle.

name: Petőfi Bridge
blurb: A long steel deck-truss bridge linking Boráros tér in Pest with Lágymányos in Buda.

name: Rákóczi Bridge
blurb: The sleek modern box-girder bridge to the south, with the National Theatre and Müpa on its Pest side.

name: Gül Baba's Tomb
blurb: The northernmost Muslim pilgrimage site in Europe, set among rose gardens.

name: Hungarian Parliament
blurb: Neo-Gothic masterpiece on the Danube bank and one of the largest parliament buildings in the world.

name: Shoes on the Danube
blurb: A moving memorial of iron shoes along the embankment, honouring Jewish victims of WWII.

name: St. Stephen's Basilica
blurb: Budapest's largest church, with a dome lookout giving a 360° view of the city.

name: Hungarian State Opera
blurb: Neo-Renaissance opera house on Andrássy Avenue with a lavish gilded interior.

name: Dohány Street Synagogue
blurb: The largest synagogue in Europe, with Moorish Revival architecture and a Holocaust memorial garden.

name: Great Market Hall
blurb: Grand neo-Gothic hall with paprika, salami, Tokaji wine, lángos upstairs and souvenirs galore.

name: Váci Street
blurb: Budapest's most famous pedestrian shopping street, running from Vörösmarty tér to the Market Hall.

name: Vörösmarty Square
blurb: Central square with the Christmas market, street performers and the historic Gerbeaud café.

name: Café Gerbeaud
blurb: Since 1858, Budapest's grandest pastry house. Try the Dobos torte.

name: New York Café
blurb: Often called the most beautiful café in the world: gilded, frescoed and unapologetically lavish.

name: Szimpla Kert
blurb: The original ruin bar: mismatched furniture, art-filled courtyards and a huge crowd after dark.

name: House of Terror
blurb: Museum on Andrássy Avenue documenting fascist and communist regimes in Hungary.

name: Liberty Square
blurb: Calm, leafy square near Parliament with fountains and the American Embassy.

name: Heroes' Square
blurb: Monumental square with the Millennium Monument: the seven chieftains, 14 kings and the Archangel Gabriel on a 36 m column, at the end of Andrássy Avenue.

name: Vajdahunyad Castle
blurb: A fairytale castle in City Park that mixes Romanesque, Gothic, Renaissance and Baroque wings, built for the 1896 millennium exhibition and home to the Agricultural Museum.

name: Széchenyi Baths
blurb: Europe's largest medicinal bath, with yellow neo-Baroque halls and outdoor pools open year-round.

name: Hungarian National Museum
blurb: Neoclassical temple of Hungarian history on Múzeum körút, where the 1848 revolution gathered on its steps; it keeps the medieval coronation mantle.

name: Hungarian Academy of Sciences
blurb: Neo-Renaissance seat of the Academy on Széchenyi tér, looking straight down the Chain Bridge.

name: Gresham Palace
blurb: Art Nouveau palace at the Pest end of the Chain Bridge, now the Four Seasons hotel, with peacock gates on its glass-roofed arcade.

name: Pesti Vigadó
blurb: Romantic-style concert hall on the Danube promenade, by Frigyes Feszl; Liszt performed here.

name: Holy Trinity Column
blurb: Baroque plague column in the middle of Szentháromság tér, between Matthias Church and the Fisherman's Bastion.

name: Sándor Palace
blurb: The President's residence on Castle Hill; the guard changes out front on the hour during the day.

name: Matthias Fountain
blurb: Bronze hunting party with King Matthias in a palace courtyard. Toss in a coin and you will come back to Budapest.

name: Hospital in the Rock
blurb: A secret WWII hospital and Cold War nuclear bunker in the caves under Castle Hill, shown on guided tours.

name: Castle Hill Funicular
blurb: The Budavári Sikló has hauled its wooden cabins from Clark Ádám tér up to the palace since 1870.

name: Zero Kilometre Stone
blurb: The sculpture all Hungarian road distances are measured from, at the foot of the funicular on Clark Ádám tér.

name: Museum of Fine Arts
blurb: Old masters from Raphael to El Greco and Goya, plus Egyptian and classical antiquities, behind a temple front on Heroes' Square.

name: Műcsarnok (Kunsthalle)
blurb: Hungary's largest hall for contemporary art, a temple-fronted gallery with a mosaic pediment on Heroes' Square.

name: Liszt Academy
blurb: Art Nouveau music academy on Liszt Ferenc tér with a gilded, Zsolnay-tiled concert hall. Catch a concert or a guided tour.

name: Rumbach Street Synagogue
blurb: Octagonal Moorish Revival synagogue designed by Otto Wagner, restored and reopened in 2021.

name: Gozsdu Courtyard
blurb: A chain of linked courtyards between Király and Dob utca, packed with bars and restaurants and lively until late.

name: Museum of Applied Arts
blurb: Ödön Lechner's Art Nouveau masterpiece under a green-and-gold Zsolnay roof. It has been under long renovation, so check before going in.

name: Müpa Budapest
blurb: The modern arts centre by the Rákóczi Bridge, home to the Béla Bartók National Concert Hall and the Ludwig Museum.

name: National Theatre
blurb: The 2002 National Theatre on the Danube bank, with a park of follies and a ziggurat lookout to climb.

name: St. Gellért Monument
blurb: The bishop raises his cross over the Elizabeth Bridge from a colonnade above a waterfall on Gellért Hill.

name: Keleti Railway Station
blurb: Grand 1884 iron-and-glass station with a huge arched window and statues of James Watt and George Stephenson.

name: Nyugati Railway Station
blurb: Iron-and-glass train shed built by the Eiffel company in 1877, with its glass front onto the Grand Boulevard.

name: House of Music Hungary
blurb: Sou Fujimoto's 2022 music centre in City Park, its roof pierced for the trees and lined underneath with golden leaves.

name: Museum of Ethnography
blurb: Folk culture from Hungary and the world in a curving 2022 building at the edge of City Park, with a roof garden you can walk up.

name: Statue of Anonymus
blurb: The hooded medieval chronicler in Vajdahunyad's courtyard. Touch his pen for a flash of writing talent.

name: Vienna Gate
blurb: The northern gate of the Castle District, rebuilt in 1936, opening onto quiet Baroque lanes.

name: St. Anne's Church
blurb: Twin-towered Baroque church on Batthyány tér, with the best street-level view of Parliament across the river.

name: Centrál Kávéház
blurb: Grand literary café from 1887 near Ferenciek tere, with high ceilings and classic Hungarian cakes.

name: Instant-Fogas
blurb: A sprawling ruin-bar complex on Akácfa utca with themed rooms, garden courtyards and several dance floors.

name: Mazel Tov
blurb: A leafy, light-strung courtyard in the old Jewish Quarter serving Israeli and Middle Eastern food.
